input.quote: (a) In the event the Company terminates this Agreement, the Company shall pay to HDI a termination payment, (the "Termination Payment") the amount of which shall be an amount equal to the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, the balance of which shall be divided by two.
input.rationale: Section 4.1 gives each Party a convenience exit at the end of each one-year term on ninety (90) days' written notice, which satisfies three of the four fallback elements (Customer notice within the 60–90 day band; HDI's right exercisable only against the annual renewal; HDI's 90-day notice). The clause fails the fallback on the fee element: Section 4.2(a) charges the Company a Termination Payment of one half of twelve months' Net Sales less $800,000 whenever the Company terminates, with no ceiling, and Section 4.2(c) makes it payable over eight quarters. That is a material penalty on our exit, far in excess of three months' fees, so we cap it at three months of the Section 3.1 payments. We are targeting the fallback rather than preferred (30 days' notice, no HDI convenience right, pro-rata refund) because the existing mutual 90-day structure is otherwise acceptable; the shorter notice and prepaid-fee refund are noted but not pressed.

proposal.summary: Cap the Termination Payment at three months of fees
proposal.comment: [Playbook] The 90-day mutual termination right in Section 4.1 works for us, but the Section 4.2 Termination Payment is an uncapped share of twelve months' Net Sales, which penalises us for leaving. We have added a cap of three months' fees under Section 3.1, which is our fallback position on early-termination fees.

ops.text: In no event shall the Termination Payment exceed the aggregate payments due from the Company to HDI pursuant to Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date.
